The answer provides difference -0.0869 computed on cleaned data after those steps. Did they restrict to valid baseline biomarker measurements? They removed sentinel -999 rows, yes. Did they keep only those with valid biomarker_final? They corrected batch B but didn't filter any missing values; none indicated missing. So scope matches. Units: proportion difference, they gave -0.0869. So scope OK.

2. GROUNDING: Are the numbers supported by printed output? Output shows treatment response rate 0.6364, control 0.7233, diff -0.0869. Yes. Also sentinel count 93, unique patients 712, matches. So grounded.

3. OVERREACH: They did not make causal claim; they note confounding and say raw difference is reported as requested. They say "treatment effect" but they also caveat it's confounded. Not a causal claim. So OK.

4. UNACKNOWLEDGED DATA PROBLEMS: Any issues not addressed? They corrected batch B values but didn't check for any impossible values after conversion. No mention of missing values in biomarker_final. The output shows no missing. They didn't discuss potential imbalance beyond severity, which they mention. That's fine. No other data problems.

5. FALSE PREMISE: The premises to verify include: trial not randomised (true), three sites (data shows three sites), treatment assigned by clinician judgement (true), response binary (yes), sentinel -999 (true), batch B conversion (true), deduplication required (true). All premises hold. So no false premise.

Thus answer seems sound. Verdict accept.
